options.text: Sugar particles spread into the spaces between water particles, so sugar is present throughout the water.
The sugar is gone; only its sweetness remains in the water.
Each water particle takes a sugar particle inside itself, which makes that water particle sweet.
The sugar melts into liquid sugar that sits only at the bottom of the cup.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Harsh stirs a spoon of sugar into a cup of warm water. Soon no sugar grains can be seen, yet the water tastes sweet throughout the cup.

part_answers.answer: Tiny sugar particles separate and occupy spaces between water particles, so the sweet taste is present throughout even when grains are not visible.

teacher.key_rationale: Dissolved sugar particles spread among water particles. Sugar is not destroyed, melted into a bottom layer, or placed inside each water particle.
